records.name: Historic Gloria Dei Preservation Corporation (Preserve Old Swedes)
records.summary: Looks after Gloria Dei (Old Swedes') Church as a historic site. It hosts history talks and concerts, runs guided tours, and offers hands-on activities that help care for the church, its graveyard, and its grounds.
records.what_you_do: Attend a Great Talk or a concert, take a guided or self-guided tour, or join a community activity such as gravestone cleaning, native gardening, bird-watching, or a crafting session.

schedule.text: Great Talks run through the year in the church sanctuary, usually 7 to 8 pm, with a meet and mingle afterward in Riverside Hall. Concerts are held on set dates. Self-guided audio tours and the graveyard map are free.

cost.text: Great Talks are ticketed and listed at $10 to $15. Concerts are listed at $15 to $30. Research requests are a $40 flat fee for up to 60 minutes. Self-guided tours are free.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for the next Great Talk through the Get Tickets link on the group's events page. Tickets are required.
first_step.basis: Talks and concerts are open to anyone who buys a ticket, and the group offers volunteer activities. The site does not say how a newcomer joins those activities.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Great Talk lasts about an hour, from 7 to 8 pm, in the church sanctuary, given by a local history expert. Afterward the speakers join a meet and mingle in Riverside Hall where they answer questions and sign books. Tickets are required and are sold through the Get Tickets link.
first_visit_tips: Buy your ticket online through the Get Tickets link before you go.
Check the events page for how many seats are left.
Stay for the meet and mingle in Riverside Hall after the talk.

records.notes: The volunteer page URL returned 404, and the community activities page shows no sign-up link or schedule. The only volunteer route found is the volunteer link on the home page, whose URL was not captured. Guided tour times and prices are not published. No page checked describes accessibility. Talk prices differ by page (the lectures page shows $10 or $12, the events page $12 and $15), so the record shows the range. Dated events are kept out of schedule text. The Mail link is a form with no published email address.

records.name: Historic Rittenhousetown
records.summary: A historic village in the Wissahickon area with a 1707 homestead, several historic houses, an arboretum, and a small museum. Visitors take tours, and volunteers and members help keep the site going.
records.what_you_do: Pull invasive plants on Wednesday morning volunteer days, take a Saturday tour of the homestead, become a member, or come to the free Second Saturday museum visits.

schedule.text: Homestead tours run on select Saturdays from Memorial Day to Labor Day, noon to 3 pm, starting on the hour. Volunteer work days are on Wednesdays, 9 am to noon. Second Saturday museum visits are free.

cost.text: Homestead tours are $10 a person, with children under 8 free, per the home page. The visit page lists pay what you wish for public tours during events. Second Saturday museum visits are free. Private tours are $20 a person, with a $50 minimum for groups of 1 to 3.

requirements.gear: Clothes for outdoor work, bug repellent, and water. Tools and gloves are provided on volunteer days.

first_step.how: Take a tour of the 1707 homestead on a select Saturday from noon to 3 pm, starting on the hour. If you want to help, email the volunteer address on the volunteer page to join a Wednesday morning work day.
first_step.basis: Tours and Second Saturday visits are open to the public, and the volunteer page gives a clear email route for joining a work day.
first_step.what_to_expect: A public homestead tour runs about 45 minutes and starts on the hour. Wednesday volunteer mornings, 9 am to noon, are outdoor work pulling invasive plants so native species can return across the 20-acre site. Tools and gloves are provided.
first_visit_tips: Arrive 5 to 10 minutes early at the Homestead entrance.
Parking is limited and on site. The main entrance is on Wissahickon Avenue.
Children under 8 go free on tours, according to the home page.
On volunteer mornings, bring water and bug repellent, since the work is outdoors.

records.notes: The group's pages disagree on tour pricing: the home page says $10 a person, and the visit page says public tours during events are pay what you wish. The volunteer page lists an individual coordinator email that looks like a personal account, so it is not recorded in contacts. The special events page has no dated 2026 items, so the active status and the 2026-10 date still rest on the tier 1 city Friends record, which was not re-checked. Fall Fest (5 to 8 pm, pay what you can) has no date in the page text. No accessibility details and no SEPTA stop are published.

records.name: Hive76
records.summary: A makerspace in Kensington where people build and learn with woodworking tools, electronics, laser cutters and 3D printers. Anyone can drop in on a Sunday open house to try the space.
records.what_you_do: Work on your own projects with shared tools and benches. Members pay a monthly fee, must be 18 or older, and sign a liability waiver before they use the space.

schedule.text: Sunday open houses run from 2 to 5 pm. Wednesday member nights run from 7 to 10:30 pm and are for members. Basic and Core members have 24-hour access.

cost.text: Light membership is $15 a month and includes tool use during open houses. Basic is $60 a month with 24-hour access. Core is $120 a month with a personal desk.

access.notes: Accessible entrance through the parking lot on Letterly St or from the Jasper St sidewalk. Call ahead so someone can let you in. The site does not describe access inside the space. Nearest SEPTA: York-Dauphin stop on the Market-Frankford Line (MFL), about a three-minute walk.

requirements.gear: Bring your own project materials. The space does not sell supplies.

first_step.how: Drop in at a Sunday open house, 2 to 5 pm, to look around. To use the tools, join as a Light member for $15 a month. Or email through the contact page for a one-on-one tour on another day.
first_step.basis: The site says beginners and experienced makers both use the space. The FAQ advises new members to come in during open hours and learn tools from experienced members, and the group holds occasional Tool-Training Days.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Sunday open house runs from 2 to 5 pm. Members work on their own projects at shared benches with shared tools, and members can ask someone experienced to teach them a tool. The Light plan is meant as a way to try the space. Ask at the door whether a visit needs a membership, since the visit page and the FAQ describe open houses a little differently.
first_visit_tips: Bring your own project materials, since the space does not sell supplies.
Take the York-Dauphin stop on the Market-Frankford Line, about three minutes away, or use the free street parking on Jasper or Hagert streets.
Ask a member or staff person to teach you a tool before you use it.
Plan to be 18 or older to join, since the group requires it for membership.

records.notes: The visit page says anyone can drop in on a Sunday open house, but the FAQ says Light members can visit during open houses and member nights, so verify at the door. Wheelchair access is set to partial because only the entrance is described as accessible. Membership is 18 or older according to the FAQ, and under 18s cannot join. The membership info and classes pages returned 404, and the join page returned an unrelated 2010 news item that was not used. No beginner class calendar was found. The newest dated item on the home page is a January 2026 post.

records.name: Hunting Park United
records.summary: A neighborhood group in Hunting Park that cleans and greens the park, plants trees and gardens, and runs family fitness days and senior programs.
records.what_you_do: Join a park cleanup, a tree or garden planting, a family fitness day, or a senior activity. Call or visit the office to ask about the next event.

schedule.text: Cleanups, tree and garden planting, fitness and family days, and senior events happen through the year, and the group announces them on its site. Office hours: Monday to Friday 9 am to 5 pm, Saturday 10 am to 2 pm, closed Sunday.

first_step.how: Call 267-800-3894, or stop by the office at 1101 W Hunting Park Ave during office hours, and ask about the next cleanup or family fitness day.
first_step.basis: Events are open to the public and the office takes calls and visits. The site does not describe membership steps, and its get involved page could not be read.
first_step.what_to_expect: Events are community days in the park: cleanups, planting trees and gardens, family fitness days, and senior activities. The site does not describe how long each event runs or what to bring, so call the office before you come.
first_visit_tips: Call the office first, since the site does not show a current event calendar.
Office hours are weekdays 9 am to 5 pm and Saturday 10 am to 2 pm. The office is closed Sunday.
Ask the office how to get there by transit, since the site does not name a SEPTA stop.

records.notes: The get involved, events, news and about pages all returned 404, so the home page and contact details are the only group pages that could be read. The home page lists a Family Fun and Fitness Day on August 8, 2026, an Oldies in the Park event on August 27, 2026, and a September 18, 2026 news post about trees tagged as a service-hours item. The email address is hidden on the home page, so the tier 1 address is kept. A web search found no 2026 event for the group. It returned only undated older articles, one of which describes a yearly cleanup that gives service letters. That is not a group page, so service_hours_letter stays unknown. The cost is not stated on the site.

records.name: Icebox Project Space
records.summary: A Philadelphia art space inside Crane Arts that shows artworks, performances, video, movement, and sound. It runs open calls for artists and holds opening receptions.
records.what_you_do: Visit an exhibit or opening reception, sign up for the newsletter, or propose a project as an artist through the online form.

schedule.text: Gallery hours are Tuesday and Wednesday 6 to 9 pm, and Friday and Saturday noon to 9 pm. Opening receptions are announced on the site.

first_step.how: Visit during gallery hours, or email iceboxprojects@gmail.com to ask about the next open call.
first_step.basis: Gallery hours and opening receptions are public, and the site gives an email address for questions. The site does not say in so many words that first-time visitors are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect a large, open room with changing work by visual artists, performers, filmmakers, and musicians. Gallery hours are set each week. Openings with receptions run from 6 to 9 pm on the dates the site posts.
first_visit_tips: The site says the space is wheelchair accessible.
Check the site for opening reception dates before you plan a visit.
Email iceboxprojects@gmail.com with questions about the next open call.

records.notes: The home page gives the July 9 opening reception (6 to 9 pm) and the June 30 open call drop-off deadline without a year. The 2026 year and the 2026-07 date are carried from tier 1 and should be checked, since the upcoming event link name includes 2026. The Light and Sound listing page shows January and February events with no years and was not used. The email in tier 1 was written with spelled out at signs; the opportunities page publishes iceboxprojects@gmail.com, which is used here. Newcomer rating is lowered from 4 to 3 because the site welcomes the public at gallery hours but does not say beginners are welcome.

records.name: Ignatian Volunteer Corps, Philadelphia and South Jersey
records.summary: Adults 50 and older give one or two days a week, September through June, to Philadelphia nonprofits that serve people in need, with monthly reflection gatherings.
records.what_you_do: Serve on site with a partner nonprofit in areas such as housing, food, tutoring, support for immigrants, and elder care, and join monthly reflection sessions with other volunteers.

schedule.text: One or two days a week, about 8 to 16 hours in total, usually September through June. Members also meet monthly with other volunteers for reflection.

first_step.how: Fill out the interest form on the IVC Philadelphia page, or email the regional office. Then you talk with the regional director about your background and availability, and IVC finds a partner nonprofit that fits.
first_step.basis: An interest form, a conversation, and a match come before you start serving, so the way in takes several steps.
first_step.what_to_expect: The first step is a conversation about your background, interests, and how many days a week you can give. Once matched, you serve one or two days a week at a nonprofit partner, usually September through June. Many members stay for several years, and you also join monthly reflection gatherings with other volunteers.
first_visit_tips: Think about which days of the week you can give before you talk with the office.
Ask the office when and where the monthly gatherings meet, since the site does not say.
Ask about transportation to the partner site, since the site does not describe it.

records.notes: Tier 1 set audience.faith to catholic. The national FAQ says there is no faith requirement and that the program welcomes people from any background who share its commitment to service and reflection, so the faith restriction is removed. The national pages describe a virtual option, but the Philadelphia page does not, so online_ok is left out. The monthly gathering day, time, and place are not published. The 2026-05 date is carried from tier 1 and was not visible on the pages re-read. The national FAQ says the service year runs 10 months and that the average member serves about 5 years.

records.name: IllReality, DBA MoveMakers Philly
records.summary: A hip hop dance school for kids and teens, ages 3 and up, with two studios on Chestnut Street. It teaches hip hop dance and music, runs after school pick up programs, and offers camps, sibling discounts, and financial aid.
records.what_you_do: Sign kids up for dance, music, or after school classes, or ask about financial aid. Range of Motion on Chestnut Street also teaches parkour and martial arts, and adult classes meet at 2100 Chestnut.

schedule.text: Youth classes and after school pick up programs run at both studios through the school year. Camps run on set days listed on the registration pages. Adult classes meet at 2100 Chestnut.

cost.text: The season registration fee is $100. Families get 30 percent off for each additional sibling, and financial aid is available by email. Class prices are on the Rates and Registration page.

first_step.how: Pick the studio for your child's class on the Rates and Registration page, then sign up on that studio's 2026 to 27 registration page. Signing up by October 30, 2026 takes 5 percent off the $100 fee. You can also email the studio about financial aid first.
first_step.basis: Beginner youth classes are listed for ages 3 and up, adult classes welcome any experience level, and the site names camps, birthday parties, and financial aid as ways to start.
first_step.what_to_expect: Youth classes are grouped by age and skill. Beginner classes are open to sign up, while intermediate, advanced, and performance classes are by invitation or after you contact the studio. Adult classes at 2100 Chestnut welcome people of any experience level. The site does not list class length or whether a trial class is offered.
first_visit_tips: Sign up by October 30, 2026 for 5 percent off the $100 fee.
Ask about financial aid or the sibling discount before you register, since the site lists both.
Confirm the studio address before you go. The Range of Motion registration link names 812 Chestnut, while its after school page lists 2100 Chestnut.

records.notes: Class and camp dates are kept out of schedule text. The youth class table lists an 11 to 18 class, so the age range runs past the 17 in the summary wording. The Range of Motion address conflicts between pages (812 vs 2100 Chestnut). The footer phone link differs from the printed number, so the printed number is kept and should be confirmed before calling. The adult classes are run under Urban Movement Arts, which is listed as a lead. Intermediate and advanced classes are by invitation or through the studio. The rates page has no class prices, and its schedule images could not be read. The email is behind a protected link on the contact page, so it is not recorded.
